title: Hepatitis B incidence per 100,000 population
national_indicator_description: As noted in the [Forward Looking Joint Health Sector Review Report for Fiscal Year 2023/2024](https://www.moh.gov.rw/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=70771&token=f73c868b77d22d7833d7762c29cde46f7ec0b4b3), this indicator is among the SDG indicators not currently monitored by the Ministry of Health. However, some information on Hepatitis B in Rwanda may be found in the [National Hepatitis Elimination Profile for Rwanda](https://www.globalhep.org/sites/default/files/content/national_profiles/files/2025-08/2025-08-06_National%20Hepatitis%20Elimination%20Profile_Rwanda.pdf) prepared by the Coalition for Global Hepatitis Elimination, and on the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Health Observatory page for [Hepatitis - new infections](https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/indicators/indicator-details/GHO/hepatitis---new-infections).
target_name: By 2030, end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases and combat hepatitis, water-borne diseases and other communicable diseases
indicator_definition: This indicator is measured indirectly through the proportion of children aged under 5 years who have developed chronic hepatitis B (HBV) infection (i.e. the proportion that tests positive for a marker of infection called hepatitis B surface antigen [HBsAg]).
